label: Thursday, November 5, 2026 · Chip hangover edition
intro: The blue-wave rally lasted one session. Wednesday the Dow posted its biggest single-day gain since April, but Thursday the AI trade gave it back as chip stocks sold off for a second day on fears the Democratic Congress tightens data-center rules.

items.title: Semiconductor ETF drops over 3% as chipmakers extend losses into a second day
items.take: The chip selloff bled through the night and into Asia, with memory giants Samsung and SK Hynix slipping hard. The fear: a Democratic sweep means tighter US data-center regulation and weaker semiconductor demand.

items.title: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq plunge in dramatic reversal, giving back post-election rally gains
items.take: A day after the Dow's biggest one-day gain since April (+1,569 points), Thursday opened with a reversal: Nasdaq down 3.6%, S&P down 2.1%, Dow down 1% intraday. Losses are concentrated in chip and data-center stocks while energy and financials hold up.

items.title: AI, data-center stocks slip as Democratic sweep clouds expansion plans
items.take: Neocloud names CoreWeave and Nebius led the slide as investors priced tougher scrutiny of data-center construction. UBS estimates about 30% of expected 2028 US data-center capacity additions could be at risk from pauses; public opposition to new facilities was already mounting.

items.title: Qualcomm plunges on weak smartphone-chip guidance; oil steadies after 8% slide
items.take: Qualcomm dropped about 10% after missing Q4 smartphone-chip estimates, hurt by sluggish demand and Apple-related revenue; global smartphone shipments fell a fifth last quarter partly on the memory-chip cost surge. Oil steadied above $95 after an 8% plunge on hopes the new Congress pressures an Iran endgame.

items.title: Voters nationwide push back against data centers
items.take: More than 20 local ballot measures to ban or restrict data centers passed Tuesday, the same night as the Democratic sweep. For the AI build-out, the resistance to new facilities is now both political and local — the backdrop behind this week's chip selloff.

items.title: Podcast: Thoughts on the Market — Solving AI's power bottleneck
items.take: This week's rotation pick lands right on the day's story: Morgan Stanley on where the power for AI data centers actually comes from, and why the bottleneck shapes which build-outs survive.
